notes: Small, curated offline list of high-impact advisories for runtimes and frameworks. It is NOT a vulnerability database: run with --osv (OSV.dev) or osv-scanner for full coverage. Each entry: affected branches as [introduced, fixed) pairs; a third element "eol" marks end-of-life lines where the upper bound is the first supported release, not a fix.

runtimes.title: PHP core remote code execution (PHP2Shell)
runtimes.summary: Memory-handling flaws in the PHP runtime. On Apache with mod_php an unauthenticated request could trigger code execution before application code ran; PHP-FPM was also confirmed exploitable through application code paths. Fixing application code or plugins does not fix it: the PHP binary must be updated.
remediation: Upgrade PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (or a distro package that backports the fix).
Rebuild and redeploy Docker images (docker build --pull).
PHP 8.1 and older have no regular upstream fix: plan the upgrade.
A WAF rule is defense in depth, not a fix.

runtimes.title: Node.js October 2026 security releases (10 CVEs, 4 high)
runtimes.summary: Includes a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can lead to crash, memory disclosure or remote code execution when an application decompresses untrusted Brotli data with node:zlib, plus TLS hostname-verification and DNS issues.
remediation: Rebuild single executable applications and startup snapshots (CVE-2026-106074).
Node.js 20 and older are end-of-life and receive no fix.

packages.title: Next.js unauthenticated RCE (use cache typed arrays, Image Optimization SVG) and Server Actions DoS
packages.summary: Two critical unauthenticated remote code execution issues (App Router 'use cache' functions returning typed arrays; Image Optimization API with SVG on glibc Linux) and a high-severity Server Actions denial of service.
remediation: Make sure the resolved sharp version is 0.35.5 or later.

eol.note: Node.js 20 and older are end-of-life and receive no security fixes.
PHP 8.1 and older receive no regular upstream security fixes.
